title: The Great Drought
tagline: The deadliest drought in modern history
body: Triggered by a record-breaking El Niño, a historic positive Indian Ocean Dipole, and unusually warm North Atlantic waters, this convergence caused near-total monsoon failure across Asia and Africa. The resulting famines in Northern China and India claimed an estimated 30 to 50 million lives — catastrophically chronicled as the 'Late Victorian Holocausts.'

title: The North American Dust Bowl
tagline: A man-made catastrophe amplified by nature
body: Driven by cool Pacific and warm Atlantic sea-surface temperatures, this drought was catastrophically amplified by decades of poor soil management. Massive 'Black Blizzard' dust storms stripped topsoil across the Great Plains, forcing millions to abandon their homes. It remains the benchmark ecological disaster of 20th-century North America.

title: The Great Sahel Drought
body: Shifting Atlantic sea-surface temperatures pushed monsoon rains steadily southward, triggering one of the most persistent structural droughts of the 20th century. The Sahara's edge advanced relentlessly across Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Chad, and Sudan. The 1983–1985 peak triggered the Ethiopian famine, sparking a landmark global humanitarian response.

title: The Millennium Drought
body: Unprecedented autumn and winter rainfall deficits dried out major river systems across southeastern Australia over twelve years. Catastrophic wildfires swept through parched landscapes, mandatory water restrictions hit every major city, and the Murray-Darling Basin nearly collapsed. The crisis fundamentally rewrote Australia's national water-security policy.

title: East African Droughts
body: By 2023, the Horn of Africa had endured five consecutive failed rainy seasons — the worst drought in 40 years. Millions of livestock perished, harvests failed entirely, and mass displacement swept across Somalia, Ethiopia, and Kenya. The crisis laid bare the acute vulnerability of the region to rising global temperatures and a climate system pushed past its limits.
